blocks.text: Verified 55+ manufactured-home parks and co-ops: what the sources show

These are the 55+ places named in public sources where you can own the home. Pad rent, shares and fees quoted below are listing-stated for one home on one date, not a park tariff, so confirm them with the park. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Sea Ridge Bays — 15875 20 Ave (King George Corridor, South Surrey)

The one verified 55+ manufactured-home community in South Surrey. Listings state "Sea Ridge Bays is 55+," "Bare land strata with low monthly fees: $210 includes water" (listing-stated fee, (with title to land recorded as Freehold Strata), a clubhouse and generous visitor parking, and that a dog owner "can have two, with no size restrictions"; another listing describes an "Age 55+ community park. Council Approval Required". There is no pad rent — the buyer owns the lot as a strata lot and pays a strata fee, so strata law, not the park tenancy Act, is the frame. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.

items.t: Manufactured-home parks run on tenancy law, not strata law: Pad tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and its Regulation (B.C. Reg. 481/2003), not the Strata Property Act — so the strata age-bylaw machinery (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, Regulation 7.01 exemptions) does not apply inside a park. A home owner must provide a purchaser with the written tenancy agreement and the written park rules, and a sale is an assignment of the pad tenancy that requires the park owner's consent.

A park's 55+ rule has its own legal footing: The MHPTA assignment rules expressly recognise a park where every pad is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 (or 2+ tenants, at least one of whom has reached 55), as set out in s. 10(2)(b)(i) of the Human Rights Code — the park owner can refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets that age requirement. That is how the three Newton / Fleetwood parks' 55+ rules operate; South Surrey has no verified pad-rent park for the rule to attach to.

Assignment consent has a clock: Under MHPTA s. 28 a tenant may assign only with the landlord's prior written consent (or consent deemed given under the regulations), an arbitrator's order, or where the tenancy agreement authorizes it; the park owner must respond within 10 days of the written request (RTB Form 10), silence counts as consent given, and no fee can be charged for consent. Before asking, the seller must give the proposed buyer written copies of the park rules and the relevant parts of the tenancy agreement.

Pad rent increases are capped: A park landlord may increase rent only with 3 full months' notice, only once every 12 months, and only up to the yearly limit — 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027; the proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of manufactured home sites in the park; further increases require a Residential Tenancy Branch application. On assignment, the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same, as does the scheduled date of a subsequent rent increase.

Park closure / conversion (MHPTA s. 42, as the Province states it): where a landlord intends to convert all or a significant part of a park to another use, the landlord must have all necessary government permits and approvals in place before issuing notice, must give 12 months' notice, and must pay the tenant $20,000 compensation on or before the notice's effective date; the tenant may move out early on at least 10 days' written notice, may dispute within 15 days, and may in defined circumstances apply for additional compensation of the home's assessed value minus the $20,000. Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw, 2025, No. 21788 does NOT apply to property governed by the MHPTA.

Registration is what makes a sale effective, and the CSA label is a sale gate: In BC, the sale, transfer or purchase of a manufactured home is only effective if registered with the Manufactured Home Registry, through a lawyer or notary filing the Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership forms. A home may not be sold unless it has the original legible CSA decal attached (Z-240 for mobile homes, A-277 for modular); if the label is lost, Technical Safety BC has a licensed electrical contractor inspect the wiring, and the electrical approval label prepared can be used in place of a CSA label. A permit to move a home is issued by the Registry and expires 30 days after issue.

Taxes on a home in a park: the Province states a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value will not include the value of the land if the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.

For contrast — the strata rule that applies at Sea Ridge Bays, not in any park: only 55+ age bylaws are legal in BC strata now (Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2; sub-55 bylaws invalid since Nov 24, 2022), the bylaw restricts who may LIVE in the unit rather than who may own it, Regulation 7.01 exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and — expanded May 1, 2023 — a younger spouse or partner, children under 19 in the specified resident's care, and adult children the specified resident cared for before they turned 19; and strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022.
City zoning: A specific park's zone is confirmed parcel by parcel in COSMOS.

OCP: Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2026, No. 21900: is the current OCP — adopted June 15, 2026, replacing Bylaw No. 18020. White Rock addresses, if any appear, fall under White Rock's own OCP Bylaw 2017, No. 2220 instead.

items.t: South Surrey's only verified 55+ manufactured-home community is not a park at all, and the clue is in its listings. Sea Ridge Bays' listings say "Council Approval Required" and record title as Freehold Strata — its buyers get strata documents and a Form B, not a tenancy agreement and park rules, and its 55+ rule is a strata bylaw with provincial exemptions a park does not offer.
This page's guide asserts more than the research could source. The rebuild should source each from the bylaw text or the operator before keeping it.
The tenure, not the structure, drives the price shape inside one feed. Individual card prices are feed data that change and are not frozen here as facts.

Two Surrey parks share almost the same name, in two different communities — and neither is in South Surrey. Westwood Court is the Fleetwood park at 8670 156 Street; Westwood Estates is the Newton park on 134 Street, whose own listings disagree on 8224 vs 8254 as the civic address. A South Surrey buyer searching "Westwood" is looking at Newton / Fleetwood product.

Surrey's tenant-protection bylaw does not cover any park on this page. Bylaw No. 21788 (2025) expressly does not apply to property governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act — park residents' redevelopment protection is the provincial s. 42 framework (permits first, 12 months' notice, $20,000 compensation).

blocks.text: South Surrey: how mobile and manufactured homes work here

items.t: Sea Ridge Bays: There is no pad rent and no MHPTA assignment step: the buyer pays a strata fee instead of pad rent, and the strata regime applies (Form B, strata fees, registered bylaws). Listings state "Sea Ridge Bays is 55+" and "Council Approval Required" — as a bare-land strata its age rule sits in the strata framework and is confirmed on its Form B.

"South Surrey" is City of Surrey ground and "White Rock" is a separate municipality with its own bylaws — the provincial tenancy framework is identical in both, but zoning claims are not interchangeable.

faq.q: How much can pad rent go up?
faq.a: Up to the yearly limit — 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — once every 12 months, on 3 full months' notice. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of sites in the park; on assignment to a new owner the rent and the next increase date carry over unchanged.

faq.q: What happens if a South Surrey park closes or is converted?
faq.a: Under s.42 of the Act, as the Province states it: the landlord must have all permits and approvals first, then give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 compensation on or before the effective date; tenants may leave early on 10 days' written notice, may dispute within 15 days, and may in defined circumstances claim additional compensation of the home's assessed value minus the $20,000; if the landlord does not proceed within a reasonable period, a further payment of the greater of $5,000 or 12 months' rent applies.

faq.q: Do I own the land under a mobile home in South Surrey?
faq.a: Usually not. In most parks you own the home and pay monthly pad rent to the park owner, and the tenancy falls under BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Ask for the tenancy agreement, the current pad rent and the park rules before you make an offer.

faq.q: Can I get a mortgage on a mobile home in South Surrey?
faq.a: Lenders look at the age of the home, whether it carries a CSA certification label and the terms of the pad tenancy, and some will not finance older homes. Speak to a mortgage broker before you write an offer, not after.

faq.q: Which South Surrey manufactured-home communities are actually 55+?
faq.a: One verifies: Sea Ridge Bays (15875 20 Ave), a bare-land strata where you own the lot — listings state "Sea Ridge Bays is 55+" and record title as Freehold Strata. No pad-rent park in South Surrey verifies as 55+; Surrey's three verified 55+ parks are in Fleetwood and Newton. The Cranley Drive community's 55+ claim is listing text only — UNVERIFIED, not counted.

faq.q: What do I own when I buy in a park, versus at Sea Ridge Bays?
faq.a: In a park, the manufactured home only — you rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, and your purchase is an assignment of that tenancy requiring the park owner's prior written consent under MHPTA s. 28, effective once registered with the Manufactured Home Registry. At Sea Ridge Bays you own the strata lot as well, pay a strata fee instead of pad rent, and close on strata documents.

faq.q: Can a park raise my pad rent when I buy, or charge me for approving me?
faq.a: No to both mechanics: on assignment the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same and the scheduled date of a subsequent increase does not change; increases otherwise need 3 full months' notice, at most once every 12 months, capped at the yearly limit (2.3% plus the proportional amount for 2026). Consent itself cannot be charged for, and the park owner must respond within 10 days of a written request — silence counts as consent.

faq.q: The live page names parks, an operator and a 50+ covenant on Cranley Drive. Can I rely on those?
faq.a: Not yet. Pull the park rules, the tenancy agreement and the title documents for the specific home before writing.

faq.q: What are the carrying costs on top of the purchase?
faq.a: Tenure decides: a park home carries pad rent (park-specific — no South Surrey pad-rent figure is published in this research, and the fee figures inside individual feed cards are listing text only); Sea Ridge Bays carries a strata fee instead — listings state $210/month including water (listing-stated, MLS®), with no pad rent. Confirm the current figure for the specific home in the tenancy agreement or Form B.

Community by community: Sea Ridge Bays listings state two dogs with no size restrictions; Westwood Court listings state pets welcome; Westwood Estates allows large dogs with park approval, no vicious breeds; Newton Mobile Home Park listings state one pet, subject to park rules. For the 160 Street and Cranley Drive communities, pet rules are UNVERIFIED — read the park rules or community documents.

faq.q: What if the home has lost its CSA label?
faq.a: A manufactured home may not be sold unless it has the original and legible CSA decal attached (Z-240 for a mobile home, A-277 for a modular). If the label is removed or lost, the home must be re-certified: Technical Safety BC arranges a licensed electrical contractor's inspection, and the electrical approval label prepared can be used in place of a CSA label to list the home for sale.

faq.q: What happens if a park is redeveloped?
faq.a: The framework is known, not open-ended: under MHPTA s. 42 the landlord must have all permits and approvals first, then give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 compensation on or before the effective date, with defined additional-compensation routes; Surrey's 2025 Tenant Protection Bylaw expressly does not cover park residents.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ pad-rental park in South Surrey?
faq.a: No verified one. Sea Ridge Bays — a bare-land strata, not a pad park — is the one verified 55+ manufactured-home community here; Breakaway Bays is NOT verified 55+ (directory 55+ vs MLS "NO AGE RESTRICTION" / "Family Park" — MLS basis governs, conflict unresolved).

faq.q: Does the park have to approve me, and can it charge for that?
faq.a: Yes to approval, no to a fee: assignment needs the park owner's prior written consent on RTB Form 10, with a response due by the 10th day and silence deemed consent; no fee may be charged for consent. Build the 10-day window into subject dates.
